A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WARC-Bench study. Their main text, tables, figures, equation, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, SFT/RLVR experiments, cross-benchmark results, behavioral analyses, and offline-training comparisons in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds planner–executor experiments, a human baseline, and desktop/mobile-only ScreenSpot evaluation.

M1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix J add a hierarchical inference procedure: a planner delegates subtasks to an SVA executor, receives completion/status feedback, and controls overall termination. This substantially extends the single-loop agent design evaluated in v1. The underlying SVA, SFT, and PPO procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The reported task and domain coverage is retained. WebArena-Lite is introduced as a filtered subset of WebArena, and the desktop/mobile ScreenSpot analysis selects previously covered domains. Humans evaluate existing Dev-Real tasks; Appendix A illustrates existing tasks rather than adding coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparator sets in Tables 2 and 3 remain unchanged. v2 adds a human reference and focused hierarchical comparisons using Qwen and Claude planners with base-model, Claude, or trained SVA executors, alongside single-loop controls in new Table 4.

E3.justification: v2 adds distinct evaluation designs: planner/executor comparisons on 165 evaluator-correctness-filtered WebArena-Lite tasks, human evaluation involving three participants on 60 Dev-Real tasks, and ScreenSpot scoring restricted to desktop/mobile screenshots. Existing training budgets, WARC-Bench splits, and original benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: New Table 4 tests the effects of hierarchical decomposition and planner/executor selection. Appendix L adds an out-of-domain grounding check, and the human evaluation discusses reading and output-format errors. Existing behavioral, latency, offline-training, and frontier-model failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 2 changes from reporting means alone to adding ± values for Dev-Total and Test results of repeatedly evaluated models. New hierarchical and human results also include ± values. The original three-run convention and OpenCUA single-run exceptions remain; additional runs are not established, and the ± statistic is not defined.

E6.justification: New results include WA-Lite success rates of 16.17% for single-loop Qwen versus 24.63% for Qwen planner/Ours executor, human accuracy of 87.11%, and desktop/mobile ScreenSpot scores in Table 7. These are additional settings, not same-setting improvements over v1. Table 2 also changes Ours-72B-RLVR Dev-Real from 78.33% to 76.67%, with the stated SFT-to-RLVR gain revised from 9.43 to 7.78 points. Original test means and Table 3 results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The subtask definition, agent formulation, and PPO objective in Equation 1 are unchanged after matching appendix renumbering. Changing the contribution wording to 'formally define' introduces no new mathematical definition, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the broad 'unique skill' contribution statement with an explicit contribution about WARC-Bench tracking long-horizon performance better than ScreenSpot V2 and MiniWoB++. This refines the main contribution framing around a finding already discussed in v1. The abstract's scientific claims and conclusion remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations about planner quality, the model-dependent benefit of hierarchical decomposition, and potentially cheaper execution with trained specialists. It also discusses human reading/formatting failures and explains the desktop/mobile restriction through uncertain ScreenSpot web-source overlap. Existing archive limitations and frontier-model failure explanations remain.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement replaces future release plans with stated repository locations for benchmark execution and training recipes. v2 also supplies the complete planner prompt, additional task examples, and explicit training-site exclusion information. Existing hyperparameters and hardware details are retained. Repository contents or availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds VisualAgentBench by Liu et al. (2024b) as the source associated with WebArena-Lite. The related-work discussion and broader positioning are largely unchanged; VisualWebBench becoming Liu et al. (2024a) is citation disambiguation.

P1.justification: There are localized contribution-list edits, additional analysis paragraphs, and new appendices for task examples, the planner prompt, and OOD evaluation. Conference headers, contact information, and cross-references are updated. Most existing prose and the overall section sequence are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4 and 7 and boxed task examples, adjusts Table 2 spacing, and adds syntax highlighting to prompt listings. Existing tables are renumbered or relocated, and figures move with pagination. The seven existing figures retain their content; there is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens benchmark validation: beyond v1's cross-benchmark comparisons, it directly tests planner/executor contributions, adds a human reference, and checks transfer on non-web screenshots. These additions address important questions about subtask usefulness, difficulty, and generalization. Repository pointers and the complete planner prompt also make reproduction more actionable. The undefined ± statistic and unmeasured inference-cost benefit limit some conclusions, but the overall evidential and reproducibility gains are substantial.
